theory.title: Repaso gramatical de la Unidad 1
theory.explanation: Esta misión integra el lenguaje trabajado en la Unidad 1: experiencias personales, hábitos y adaptación, arrepentimiento, planes futuros, estilo indirecto, relativas, gerundios e infinitivos y tiempos narrativos. No introduce estructuras nuevas. El objetivo es combinar los recursos con claridad para contar experiencias, describir personas, explicar decisiones y transmitir conversaciones.
theory.tip: Elige la estructura según lo que quieras expresar: experiencia, hábito, consejo sobre el pasado, plan, información transmitida o secuencia narrativa.

patterns.label: Experiencias vitales
patterns.pattern: Have you ever travelled alone? / I visited Rome last year.
examples:
Have you ever travelled alone? / I visited Rome last year.
→ ¿Has viajado alguna vez solo/a? / Fui a Roma el año pasado.

patterns.label: Hábitos pasados y adaptación
patterns.pattern: I used to be shy. / I'm getting used to speaking in public.
examples:
I used to be shy. / I'm getting used to speaking in public.
→ Antes era tímido/a. / Me estoy acostumbrando a hablar en público.

patterns.label: Arrepentimientos pasados
patterns.pattern: I should have checked the details. / I could have asked for help.
examples:
I should have checked the details. / I could have asked for help.
→ Debería haber comprobado los detalles. / Podría haber pedido ayuda.

patterns.label: Planes de futuro
patterns.pattern: I'm going to apply for a course. / I might travel next summer.
examples:
I'm going to apply for a course. / I might travel next summer.
→ Voy a solicitar un curso. / Quizá viaje el próximo verano.

patterns.label: Afirmaciones en estilo indirecto
patterns.pattern: She said she had enjoyed the experience.
examples:
She said she had enjoyed the experience.
→ Ella dijo que había disfrutado de la experiencia.

patterns.label: Preguntas en estilo indirecto
patterns.pattern: He asked whether I was available.
examples:
He asked whether I was available.
→ Él preguntó si estaba disponible.

patterns.label: Oraciones de relativo
patterns.pattern: A person who inspires me… / The town where I grew up…
examples:
A person who inspires me… / The town where I grew up…
→ Una persona que me inspira… / El pueblo donde crecí…

patterns.label: Gerundios
patterns.pattern: I enjoy meeting new people. / She suggested taking a break.
examples:
I enjoy meeting new people. / She suggested taking a break.
→ Disfruto conociendo gente nueva. / Ella sugirió hacer una pausa.

patterns.label: Infinitivos
patterns.pattern: We decided to move. / I went there to learn.
examples:
We decided to move. / I went there to learn.
→ Decidimos mudarnos. / Fui allí para aprender.

patterns.label: Tiempos narrativos
patterns.pattern: I was walking when… / By the time I arrived, it had started.
examples:
I was walking when… / By the time I arrived, it had started.
→ Estaba caminando cuando… / Para cuando llegué, ya había empezado.

content.passage: Over the past few years, I have had several experiences which changed the way I see the world. I used to avoid new situations, but a teacher who believed in me encouraged me to join a local project. At first, I found it difficult to speak to strangers. One afternoon, while I was helping at an event, I realised that I had left an important box at home. I should have checked the list before leaving. A colleague offered to drive me back and told me that we still had enough time. Later, the organiser asked whether I could help with another event. I decided to say yes because I enjoy meeting people and learning new skills. By the time the project finished, I had made several friends and become more confident. Looking back, I can see that one small decision led to an opportunity which I would never have expected.

items.prompt: Describe an experience that has changed you.
items.modelAnswer: A few years ago, I started a new job which helped me become more independent. At first I was nervous, but my colleagues encouraged me. Looking back, I can see that the experience changed my confidence.

items.prompt: Talk about a person who has influenced your life.
items.modelAnswer: My aunt is someone who has always supported me. She told me that I should try new things and reminded me not to give up when something was difficult.

items.prompt: Describe a decision you made and what happened afterwards.
items.modelAnswer: I decided to join a language class because I wanted to communicate more confidently. I used to feel shy, but I have made friends and improved a lot.

items.prompt: Retell a conversation using reported speech.
items.modelAnswer: My friend told me she had found a new flat. She said it was close to work and asked whether I wanted to visit. I told her I would go the following weekend.

items.prompt: Tell a short story about an unexpected event.
items.modelAnswer: I was walking to the station when I realised I had left my wallet at home. By the time I returned, I had missed my train, but I eventually caught the next one.

items.prompt: Describe a habit you used to have and how it changed.
items.modelAnswer: I used to stay up late watching television. I decided to go to bed earlier because I wanted more energy. Now I'm used to getting up early.

items.prompt: Talk about something you regret and what you learned.
items.modelAnswer: I once agreed to organise an event without asking for help. I should have shared the tasks with other people. Since then, I plan more carefully.

items.prompt: Describe a person or place using a relative clause.
items.modelAnswer: My best friend, who lives nearby, is someone I can always rely on. We often meet in a café where we first studied together.

items.prompt: Explain a goal you are planning to achieve.
items.modelAnswer: I'm going to improve my English this year. I plan to practise every day and hope to feel more confident when I travel.

items.prompt: Summarise what you have learned in this unit.
items.modelAnswer: I've learned to talk about life experiences, describe people, explain decisions and tell stories clearly. I've also practised reporting conversations and connecting ideas with more complex grammar.

content.audioTranscript: Ella: Have you ever taken part in a community project? Mark: Yes. I joined one last year because I wanted to meet people who lived nearby. Ella: What did you use to do before that? Mark: I used to spend most weekends at home, but my neighbour encouraged me to volunteer. Ella: What happened on your first day? Mark: I was helping in the garden when it started to rain. By the time we finished, everyone was covered in mud. Ella: Did you enjoy it? Mark: I did. The organiser told me that the group had planned another event and asked whether I could come. Ella: What did you say? Mark: I said I would try. I've decided to keep volunteering because I enjoy doing something useful. Ella: That's a great way to make new memories.
